en.greeting: Hi again! Today we build your first word bank: everyday people, places and things, numbers from 1 to 20, and simple colours and adjectives. Small groups of words, one step at a time.

steps.title: Everyday nouns
steps.text: Let's start with words you use every day: people, places and things.
steps.body:
**People:** mother, father, friend, teacher. **Places:** house, school, office, market. **Things:** phone, book, table, water.

Learn each word with **a** or **an**: a book, a house, but **an** office (because office starts with a vowel sound).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Quick check on places. Pick the right word.

question.prompt: Complete: My mother buys vegetables at the ___. (pasar)
question.explanation: **pasar** = **market**. An office is kantor and a school is sekolah.

steps.title: Numbers 1–20
steps.text: Now numbers. You need them for prices, ages and phone numbers.
steps.body:
**1–10:** one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. **11** eleven and **12** twelve have their own names.

**13–19** end in **-teen**. Watch the spelling: **thir**teen (not 'threeteen'), **fif**teen (not 'fiveteen'). **20** is twenty.

Stress the end: thir-**TEEN** (13). If you say **THIR**-ty, people hear 30.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Use the -teen rule for this one.

question.prompt: There are 19 students in my class. How do you write 19 in words?
question.explanation: 13–19 end in **-teen**, so 19 = **nineteen**. Ninety is 90, and nineten is a spelling mistake.

steps.title: Colours and adjectives go first
steps.text: Here is the big difference from Indonesian: the describing word comes first.
steps.body:
Indonesian says 'mobil merah'; English says **a red car**. Colours and other adjectives come **before** the noun.

They also never take **-s**: 'two new phones', not 'two news phones'.

steps.title: In real life
steps.text: Here's how these words work together at the shop, at school and on the phone.
steps.body: In phone numbers, English speakers often say 0 as **oh**.

examples.en: The blue bag is twelve dollars.
examples.id: Tas biru itu dua belas dolar.

examples.en: I want the big one, please.
Our school has a green door.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Put the words in order. Remember where the adjective goes.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ayahku punya telepon baru.
question.solution: My father has a new phone.
question.explanation: The adjective **new** comes **before** the noun: a new phone (Indonesian: telepon baru).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: One more about word order and -s.

question.prompt: At a café you want 'teh panas'. What do you say? "___, please."
question.explanation: The adjective goes first and never takes -s: **hot tea**. 'Tea hot' follows Indonesian order.

steps.title: Flashcards
steps.text: Flip through these to review. Say each one out loud.

id.greeting: Hai lagi! Hari ini kita membangun kosakata pertamamu: orang, tempat dan benda sehari-hari, angka 1 sampai 20, serta warna dan kata sifat sederhana. Sedikit demi sedikit, satu langkah sekali jalan.

steps.title: Kata benda sehari-hari
steps.text: Kita mulai dari kata yang kamu pakai setiap hari: orang, tempat dan benda.
steps.body:
**Orang:** mother, father, friend, teacher. **Tempat:** house, school, office, market. **Benda:** phone, book, table, water.

Pelajari setiap kata bersama **a** atau **an**: a book, a house, tapi **an** office (karena office diawali bunyi vokal).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Cek cepat soal tempat. Pilih kata yang tepat.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: My mother buys vegetables at the ___. (pasar)
question.explanation: **pasar** = **market**. Office itu kantor, dan school itu sekolah.

steps.title: Angka 1–20
steps.text: Sekarang angka. Kamu butuh ini untuk harga, umur dan nomor telepon.
steps.body:
**1–10:** one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. **11** eleven dan **12** twelve punya nama sendiri.

**13–19** berakhiran **-teen**. Perhatikan ejaannya: **thir**teen (bukan 'threeteen'), **fif**teen (bukan 'fiveteen'). **20** adalah twenty.

Tekan bagian akhirnya: thir-**TEEN** (13). Kalau kamu bilang **THIR**-ty, orang mendengar 30.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pakai aturan -teen untuk soal ini.

question.prompt: There are 19 students in my class. Bagaimana menulis 19 dengan huruf?
question.explanation: 13–19 berakhiran **-teen**, jadi 19 = **nineteen**. Ninety itu 90, dan nineten salah ejaan.

steps.title: Warna dan sifat di depan
steps.text: Ini bedanya yang paling besar dengan bahasa Indonesia: kata sifatnya ada di depan.
steps.body:
Bahasa Indonesia bilang 'mobil merah'; bahasa Inggris bilang **a red car**. Warna dan kata sifat lain diletakkan **sebelum** kata benda.

Kata sifat juga tidak pernah ditambah **-s**: 'two new phones', bukan 'two news phones'.

steps.title: Dalam kehidupan nyata
steps.text: Begini kata-kata ini dipakai bersama di toko, di sekolah dan di telepon.
steps.body: Dalam nomor telepon, penutur bahasa Inggris sering menyebut 0 sebagai **oh**.

examples.en: The blue bag is twelve dollars.
examples.id: Tas biru itu dua belas dolar.

examples.en: I want the big one, please.
Our school has a green door.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Urutkan kata-katanya. Ingat di mana kata sifat diletakkan.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ayahku punya telepon baru.
question.solution: My father has a new phone.
question.explanation: Kata sifat **new** diletakkan **sebelum** kata benda: a new phone (bahasa Indonesia: telepon baru).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Satu lagi soal urutan kata dan -s.

question.prompt: Di kafe kamu mau 'teh panas'. Apa yang kamu ucapkan? "___, please."
question.explanation: Kata sifat diletakkan di depan dan tidak pernah ditambah -s: **hot tea**. 'Tea hot' mengikuti urutan bahasa Indonesia.

steps.title: Kartu hafalan
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini untuk mengulang. Ucapkan masing-masing dengan suara keras.
